title: Short-Term Anesthesia of Calliphora Larvae Using Isobutane Vapors
author: Evhenii Hordiienko

steps.title: Prepare Larva in Chamber
steps.instruction: Place the Calliphora larva onto a dry substrate at the bottom of a 45 mL exposure chamber.

steps.title: Collect Liquid Isobutane
steps.instruction: Draw exactly 5 mL of liquid phase gas from a liquefied isobutane canister using a medical syringe.

substeps.instruction: Press the canister valve directly into the syringe nozzle (without a needle)
Draw 5 mL of liquid phase gas

steps.title: Inject Gas and Seal Chamber
steps.instruction: Rapidly inject the liquid gas into the chamber and seal it to begin the exposure period.

substeps.instruction: Slightly open the exposure chamber cap
Inject the liquid gas from the syringe onto the inner wall of the container, avoiding contact with the larva
Immediately close the cap tightly to ensure hermetic sealing

steps.title: Monitor for Akinesia
steps.instruction: Perform visual observation to record the onset of akinesia, which occurs on average at the 40th second from sealing.

steps.title: Terminate Exposure and Recover Larva
steps.instruction: Limit total residency time in the chamber to 50 seconds, then remove the larva.

substeps.instruction: Quickly retrieve the larva and transfer it to fresh air (or perform forced ventilation of the chamber)

steps.title: Observe Initial Recovery
steps.instruction: Allow the larva to recover in fresh air; complete restoration of locomotor functions is achieved on average after 1 minute and 5 seconds.

steps.title: Prepare for Second Exposure
steps.instruction: Place the same larva back into the chamber, ensuring it is cleared of any residual gas mixture from the previous run.

steps.title: Repeat Isobutane Injection
steps.instruction: Repeat the process of drawing and injecting 5 mL of liquid isobutane as performed in the first phase.

steps.title: Monitor Accelerated Akinesia
steps.instruction: Observe the onset of akinesia, which occurs faster during this phase, on average at the 20th second.

steps.title: Terminate Second Exposure
steps.instruction: Limit the maximum allowable cumulative time inside the chamber during this phase to 1 minute and 30 seconds, then retrieve the object and transfer it to fresh air.

steps.title: Observe Final Recovery Dynamics
steps.instruction: Monitor the recovery of functions in fresh air according to the following timeline:

substeps.instruction: At 30 seconds: Record first signs of activity (slight twitching, body contractions)
At 2 minutes: Confirm full and deep restoration of all locomotor and physiological functions
